segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that his hour had come to pass from this world to the Father; having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And during supper, when the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to hand him over,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: got up from supper, laid aside his outer garments, and, taking a linen towel, tied it around his waist.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he poured water into the basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to dry them with the towel that was tied around him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he came to Simon Peter, who said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, are you going to wash my feet?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You do not know now what I am doing, but afterward you will understand.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You will never, ever wash my feet!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Unless I wash you, you have no share with me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “One who has bathed has no need to wash, except for the feet, but is clean all over. And you are clean, but not all of you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For he knew who was handing him over; that is why he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Not all of you are clean.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when he had washed their feet, put his outer garments back on, and reclined again, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you understand what I have done for you?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You call me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and you are right to say so, for that is what I am.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So if I, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I have given you an example, so that you also should do just as I have done for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly I tell you, a slave is not greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am not speaking about all of you; I know the ones I have chosen. But this is so that the scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one who eats my bread has lifted up his heel against me.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am telling you now, before it happens, so that when it does happen you may believe that I am he.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly I tell you, whoever receives anyone I send receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had said this, Jesus was troubled in spirit and testified,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly I tell you, one of you will hand me over.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples looked at one another, at a loss as to whom he meant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of his disciples, the one Jesus loved, was reclining at Jesus’s side.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Simon Peter nodded to him to ask who it was that he was speaking about.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That disciple, leaning back just as he was against Jesus’s chest, said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, who is it?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “It is the one for whom I will dip the piece of bread and give it to him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So, having dipped the piece of bread, he gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And after the piece of bread, Satan then entered into him. So Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What you are doing, do quickly.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But none of those reclining at the table knew why he said this to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Some supposed, since Judas kept the money box, that Jesus was telling him, “Buy what we need for the festival,” or that he should give something to the poor.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So, having taken the piece of bread, he went out at once. And it was night.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had gone out, Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him at once.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for me, and just as I told the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come,’ so now I say it to you as well.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: A new commandment I give you: that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, where are you going?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Where I am going you cannot follow me now, but you will follow later.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly I tell you, a rooster will not crow until you have denied me three times.”

notes.note: The Greek phrase can mean 'to the end' in time (to the last moment of his life) or 'to the utmost, completely'. Both senses are well attested, and many scholars think John intends both. 'To the end' is kept because it leaves room for either reading.

The verb means 'hand over' or 'deliver up'; it is the ordinary word for delivering someone into custody, and Greek has a separate verb for 'betray'. English tradition renders it 'betray' whenever Judas is the subject, which is a fair inference from the story but narrower than the word itself. The same verb is used elsewhere of the authorities handing Jesus over to Pilate.

notes.phrase: put it into the heart of Judas
notes.traditional: put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray him
notes.note: In the best-attested Greek text the wording is literally 'the devil having already put into the heart that Judas should hand him over', without saying whose heart. Most translators take it as Judas's heart; some scholars take it as the devil's own, meaning the devil had already resolved on it. Later manuscripts reword the phrase so that it is unambiguously Judas's heart.

The verb for 'laid aside' is the one this Gospel uses for Jesus laying down his life (10:11–18) and for Peter's offer in verses 37–38. The verb for putting the garments back on in verse 12 is the one used there for taking his life up again. Many commentators think the echo is deliberate and that the footwashing acts out his death in advance.

A few early witnesses, including Codex Sinaiticus, lack these words and read simply 'has no need to wash'. Most manuscripts include them, and most editors and translations keep them, though some scholars regard the shorter text as original.

The Greek word denotes a person owned by another, not a hired servant, and a first-century reader would have heard it that way. 'Servant' is the traditional English rendering, and some modern versions keep it. The word for 'master' here is the same one translated 'Lord' in verses 13–14, so the saying applies directly to Jesus and his disciples.

The Greek word is the one elsewhere rendered 'apostle'. This is its only occurrence in John's Gospel, and here it carries its ordinary sense of someone sent on another's behalf, not the title of an office.

notes.phrase: has lifted up his heel against me
notes.traditional: hath lifted up his heel against me
notes.note: The quotation is from Psalm 41:9, where the speaker is betrayed by a close friend who shared his table. Eating someone's bread implied a bond of loyalty, so the image is of treachery from within the circle of trust. The exact force of 'lifting the heel' is uncertain; it is usually taken as a gesture of contempt or a hostile kick.

The Greek is simply 'I am', with no complement. It can mean 'I am the one I claim to be', but it also echoes God's self-declaration in the Greek version of Isaiah (for example 43:10, 'that you may know and believe that I am'). Many scholars hold that John intends the divine echo here; some translations therefore print 'I am'.

At formal meals diners reclined on their left side on low couches, so the person on one's right lay with his head near one's chest; this is how the disciple can lean back and speak privately in verse 25. The Greek says literally 'in Jesus's bosom', the same expression used in 1:18 of the Son's place with the Father.

notes.phrase: If God has been glorified in him
notes.traditional: If God be glorified in him
notes.note: This opening clause is absent from several of the earliest and best manuscripts. It may have been dropped accidentally because it repeats the end of the previous verse, or added later to smooth the logic. The edition translated here includes it, and scholars remain divided.

candidates.reason: It recurs throughout the Gospels and Paul for Judas, the authorities and God alike, and translators split between 'betray' and 'hand over', so readers would see the English vary for one Greek word.
It is frequent across the New Testament and the choice between 'slave' and 'servant' materially changes how readers hear both parables and the apostles' self-descriptions.
Jesus's formula (doubled in John, single in the Synoptics) needs one fixed rendering, since translators vary between 'truly', 'very truly', 'amen' and 'I assure you'.
The same word covers 'sir', 'master' and 'Lord', and a rule is needed for where each applies, especially in address to Jesus and in sayings like 13:16 that play on the overlap.
It is rendered 'life' or 'soul' in different contexts across the New Testament, and inconsistent choices mislead readers about what is being laid down, lost or saved.
